success_patterns: Compare map claims along separate axes—group invariance, rational versus regular extension, pole-locus constraints, and fiber structure—instead of treating stronger structural properties as automatic.

When asked for the strongest valid statement, retain the supported invariant rational-map claim while rejecting additional regularity or orbit-classification requirements unless each is independently established.

patch.reasoning: The successful choice preserves the supported existence and invariance claims without adding unverified conditions on regularity, poles, or fibers. The skill already emphasizes logical strength and unsupported strengthenings; making these map-specific axes explicit can help distinguish nested existence options.

edits.content: - For maps specified on an open locus, compare separately group invariance, rational extension to the ambient space, regularity everywhere, pole-locus constraints, and fiber descriptions. Agreement on an open locus does not by itself establish regularity or special pole or fiber structure; justify each added property independently.
